gloss: you
glosses: you
etym: From Proto-Vietic *ŋaːj, from Proto-Mon-Khmer *[m]ŋaaj (“human being; person”). Cognate with Muong ngài, Bahnar bơngai (“people, human being”) and Pacoh ngai (“they; them; their; others”). Also from the same root is ngươi (“pupil”).

etym: Sino-Vietnamese word from 婆 (“grandmother”). In Chinese and Japanese, the male counterpart would be 爺 /爷 (yé, “grandfather”), but Vietnamese ông derives from 翁 (“old man”) instead.

gloss: I/me
glosses: I/me
etym:
Attested as mềnh, mình, in the Dictionarium Annamiticum Lusitanum et Latinum (1651).
The form mềnh appears to be more conservative and was widely used in the Northern dialects, while the now common form mình seems to be originally Central-S
